content: 1. Martin P, Carosi G, et al. investigated the relapse of hepatitis B in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients who discontinued successful entecavir treatment. Their findings support the case for continuous antiviral therapy. Published in the Journal of Hepatology, 2009; 50(2):289–95. 2. Kim YJ, Kim K, Hwang SH, et al. examined the durability of response after discontinuation of nucleos(t)ide therapy in chronic HBeAg-negative hepatitis B patients. Published in Clinical and Molecular Hepatology, 2013; 19(3):300–4. 3. Reijnders JG, Perquin MJ, Zhang N, et al. demonstrated that nucleos(t)ide analogues induce only temporary hepatitis B e antigen seroconversion in most patients with chronic hepatitis B. Published in Gastroenterology, 2010; 139(2):491–8. 4. Song MJ, Song DS, Kim HY, et al. studied the durability of viral response after off-treatment in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B patients. Published in World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2012; 18(43):6277–83. 5. Chaung KT, Ha NB, Trinh HN, et al. reported a high frequency of recurrent viremia after hepatitis B e antigen seroconversion and consolidation therapy. Published in Journal of Clinical Gastroenterology, 2012; 46(10):865–70. 6. Fung SK, Andreone P, Han SH, et al. highlighted that adefovir-resistant hepatitis B can be associated with viral rebound and hepatic decompensation. Published in Journal of Hepatology, 2005; 43(6):937–43. 7. Fontana RJ, Hann HW, Perrillo RP, et al. identified determinants of early mortality in patients with decompensated chronic hepatitis B treated with antiviral therapy. Published in Gastroenterology, 2002; 123(3):719–27. 8. Chien RN, Lin CH, Liaw YF. explored the effect of lamivudine therapy in hepatic decompensation during acute exacerbation of chronic hepatitis B. Published in Journal of Hepatology, 2003; 38(3):322–7. 9. Lim SG, Wai CT, Rajnakova A, et al. documented fatal hepatitis B reactivation following discontinuation of nucleoside analogues for chronic hepatitis B. Published in Gut, 2002; 51(4):597–9. 10. Prati D, Taioli E, Zanella A, et al. provided updated definitions of healthy ranges for serum alanine aminotransferase levels. Published in Annals of Internal Medicine, 2002; 137(1):1–10. 11. Andersson KL, Chung RT. discussed monitoring during and after antiviral therapy for hepatitis B. Published in Hepatology, 2009; 49(5 Suppl):S166–S173. 12. Chu CM, Liaw YF. identified predictive factors for reactivation of hepatitis B following hepatitis B e antigen seroconversion in chronic hepatitis B. Published in Gastroenterology, 2007; 133(5):1458–65. 13. Brunetto MR, Oliveri F, Colombatto P, et al. demonstrated that hepatitis B surface antigen serum levels help distinguish active from inactive hepatitis B virus genotype D carriers. Published in Gastroenterology, 2010; 139(2):483–90. 14. Liang J, Tang YF, Wu FS, et al. conducted a systematic review comparing entecavir versus lamivudine for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B. Published in Pharmazie, 2012; 67(11):883–90. 15. Liu H, Wang X, Wan G, et al. performed a meta-analysis comparing telbivudine versus entecavir for nucleos(t)ide-naïve HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B. Published in American Journal of Medical Sciences, 2014; 347(2):131–8. 16. Su QM, Ye XG. conducted a meta-analysis on the effects of telbivudine and entecavir for HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B. Published in World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2012; 18(43):6290–301. 17. Ye XG, Su QM. performed a meta-analysis on the effects of entecavir and lamivudine for hepatitis B decompensated cirrhosis. Published in World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2013; 19(39):6665–78. 18. Heo J, Park JY, Lee HJ, et al. conducted a 96-week randomized trial of switching to entecavir in chronic hepatitis B patients with a partial virological response to lamivudine. Published in Antiviral Therapy, 2012; 17(8):1563–70. 19. Hyun JJ, Seo YS, Yoon E, et al. compared the efficacies of lamivudine versus entecavir in patients with hepatitis B virus-related decompensated cirrhosis. Published in Liver International, 2012; 32(4):656–64. 20. Bang SJ, Kim BG, Shin JW, et al. studied the clinical course of patients with insufficient viral suppression during entecavir therapy in genotype C chronic hepatitis B. Published in Digestive and Liver Disease, 2013; 45(7):600–5. 21. Hass HG, Bock T, Nehls O, et al. identified that a rapid HBV DNA decrease at week 12 is an important prognostic factor for first-line treatment with adefovir dipivoxil for chronic hepatitis B. Published in Journal of Gastroenterology, 2009; 44(8):871–7. 22. Reijnders JG, Leemans WF, Hansen BE, et al. demonstrated that virologic response during adefovir therapy in chronic hepatitis B can be assessed at 24 weeks. Published in Journal of Viral Hepatitis, 2009; 16(2):113–20. 23. McMahon BJ, Bulkow L, Simons B, et al. explored the relationship between hepatitis B virus DNA levels and liver disease in a population-based study of HBeAg-negative individuals. Published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, 2014; 12(4):701–6. 24. Tohme RA, Bulkow L, Homan CE, et al. analyzed rates and risk factors for hepatitis B reactivation in a cohort of individuals in the inactive phase of chronic hepatitis B. Published in Journal of Clinical Virology, 2013; 58(2):396–400. 25. Papatheodoridis GV, Manolakopoulos S, Liaw YF, et al. reviewed follow-up and indications for liver biopsy in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B virus infection with persistently normal ALT. Published in Journal of Hepatology, 2012; 57(1):196–202. 26. Tai DI, Lin SM, Sheen IS, et al. examined the long-term outcome of HBeAg-negative hepatitis B surface antigen carriers in relation to changes in alanine aminotransferase levels over time. Published in Hepatology, 2009; 49(6):1859–67. 27. Feld JJ, Ayers M, El-Ashry D, et al. developed hepatitis B virus DNA prediction rules for HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B. Published in Hepatology, 2007; 46(4):1057–70.
